chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abī Baṣīr, from ʿImrān ibn Maytham or Ṣāliḥ ibn Maytham, from his father, who said:

A woman who was pregnant came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I have committed zina, so purify me—may Allah purify you—for the punishment of this world is easier than the punishment of the Hereafter that does not cease.” He said to her, “From what shall I purify you?” She said, “I have committed zina.” He said to her, “Are you married, or otherwise?” She said, “Rather, I am married.” He said to her, “Was your husband present when you did what you did, or was he absent from you?” She said, “Rather, he was present.” He said to her, “Go and deliver what is in your womb, then come to me and I will purify you.” When the woman turned away from him and reached a place where she could no longer hear his speech, he said: “O Allah, it is one testimony.”

Before long, she came and said: “I have delivered, so purify me.” He said: so he acted as though unaware and said, “O maidservant of Allah, from what is that?” She said, “I have committed zina, so purify me.” He said, “Were you married when you did what you did?” She said, “Yes.” He said, “Was your husband present or absent?” She said, “Rather, he was present.” He said, “Go and nurse him for two complete years, as Allah has commanded you.” He said: so the woman departed, and when she had reached a place where she could no longer hear his speech, he said: “O Allah, they are two testimonies.” He said: when two years had passed, the woman came and said: “I have nursed him for two years, so purify me, O Amīr al-Muʾminīn.” So he acted as though unaware of her and said, “Shall I purify you from what?” She said, “I have committed zina, so purify me.” He said, “Were you married when you did what you did?” She said, “Yes.” He said, “And was your husband absent when you did what you did, or present?” She said, “Rather, he was present.” He said, “Go and care for him until he understands how to eat and drink and does not fall from a roof and does not plunge into a well.” He said: so she departed while weeping, and when she turned to where she could no longer hear his speech, he said: “O Allah, it is three testimonies.”

Then ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth al-Makhzūmī met her and said: “What makes you weep, O maidservant of Allah, when I have seen you going repeatedly to ʿAlī عليه السلام asking him to purify you?” She said: “I came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and asked him to purify me, and he said: ‘Care for your child until he understands how to eat and drink and does not fall from a roof and does not plunge into a well,’ and I have feared that death may come upon me before he purifies me.” So ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth said to her: “Return to him, for I will take care of him.” So she returned and informed Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام of what ʿAmr had said. Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said to her, acting as though unaware of her: “And why would ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth take care of your child?” She said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I have committed zina, so purify me.” He said: “Were you married when you did what you did?” She said: “Yes.” He said: “Was your husband absent when you did what you did, or present?” She said: “Rather, he was present.”

He said: then he raised his head to the sky and said: “O Allah, four testimonies have now been established for You against her, and You have said to Your Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله: O Muḥammad, whoever suspends one of My prescribed punishments has opposed Me and thereby sought to resist Me. O Allah, I am not one who suspends Your limits, nor one who seeks to oppose You, nor one who neglects Your rulings; rather, I am obedient to You and a follower of the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of Your Prophet.” He said: then ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth looked at him, and it was as though pomegranates were bursting in his face. When ʿAmr saw that, he said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I only intended to care for him when I thought that you would like that, but now that you dislike it, I will not do it.” So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “After four testimonies by Allah, you shall certainly care for him while humbled.”

Then Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ascended the pulpit and said: “O Qanbar, call among the people: al-salat (prayer) is to be held collectively.” So Qanbar called among the people, and they gathered until the mosque was filled with its people. Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام stood, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: “O people, your Imam is going out with this woman to this open ground to carry out the hadd upon her, if Allah wills. Amīr al-Muʾminīn has bound you that you do not go out except while disguised, and with your companions, such that none of you recognizes another, until you return to your homes, if Allah wills.” He said: then he descended.

Then when the people came in the morning, he went out with the woman, and the people went out disguised, veiled with their turbans and cloaks, with stones in their cloaks and sleeves, until he reached with her—and the people with him—the outskirts of al-Kūfah. He ordered that a pit be dug for her, then he buried her in it. Then he mounted his mule and fixed his foot in the stirrup-ring, then placed his two index fingers in his ears, then called out in the loudest of his voice: “O people, Allah the Exalted entrusted His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله with a covenant, which Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله entrusted to me: that one upon whom there is a hadd owed to Allah should not carry out the hadd. So whoever owes to Allah a hadd like that which she owes should not carry out the hadd upon her.” He said: so all the people departed that day except Amīr al-Muʾminīn and al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام. So these three carried out the hadd upon her that day, and there was no one with them besides them. He said: and among those who departed that day was Muḥammad son of Amīr al-Muʾminīn. Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from Khālid ibn Ḥammād, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: “A pregnant woman came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and said: I have done it, so purify me,” and he mentioned something similar.

key_terms.أَرْضِعِيهِ: Nurse him; instruction to breastfeed the child
key_terms.اكْفُلِيهِ: Take care of him; maintain and protect the child until independent safety
key_terms.ذَاتُ بَعْلٍ: A married woman; one who has a husband
key_terms.زَنَيْتُ: I committed zina; the woman’s explicit confession to illicit intercourse
key_terms.سُنَّةَ نَبِيِّكَ: The sunnah (prophetic tradition) of Your Prophet; the normative practice being followed
key_terms.شَهَادَاتٍ: Testimonies; repeated confessional statements establishing the case
key_terms.فَطَهِّرْنِي: Purify me; meaning to subject her to the legal punishment she believed would cleanse her of sin

ai.seo_question: How did Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام deal with a pregnant woman who repeatedly confessed to zina?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates how Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام repeatedly delayed the legal punishment of a woman who confessed to zina until her child’s rights of birth, nursing, and care were secured. It also describes the eventual establishment of the hadd after four confessions and the careful public procedure followed in carrying it out.
